roguelike_editor

roguelike_editor is a tool for creating data for roguelike games.
You can launch roguelike_editor by double-clicking /tools/roguelike_editor/tvpwin32.exe or /tools/roguelike_editor/data/run.bat.

When launched, the control window will be displayed as shown below.
Click the buttons to launch the respective editors.
Hovering the cursor over the label of each editor displays tooltips for your reference.



Map Editor

Allows you to create rooms to place on the map.
First, create the map chips.
Please place the map chips in the /tools/roguelike_editor/data/mapchips/ folder.
In addition, make sure to create all map chips at the exact same size.



Settings for each chip are located on the right side of the window.
You can assign any arbitrary name to the chip in "Name".
This name is not currently used, but setting it now may be useful for the future.
"Chip Type" specifies the type of chip.
It defines which part of the room the chip belongs to.
The "Wall" type is particularly important and always required.

Chips with the "Walkable" checkbox checked are recognized as walkable floors.
These walkable chips are also important and always required.

In "Group", specify a unique Group ID for the chip.
Create a room using only chips that share the same Group ID specified here.
Fill a single room using chips of a single Group ID.
Rooms placed on a single floor will consist only of rooms with the same Group ID.
The Group ID is used to ensure a single floor map consists only of rooms with matching designs.
Rooms with different designs should be assigned different Group IDs to maintain visual consistency.

Finally, clicking the Save button saves the chip information to /tools/roguelike_editor/data/mapdata/roguelike_mapchips.dic.
Place this file in your project folder and load it via script.




Clicking a chip displayed in the Map Chip window selects it, and clicking any cell in the Map Editor places the chip.

Room dimensions can be adjusted via the "Settings" button.
The "Fill" button enables the fill tool.
Dragging and dropping a chip from the Map Chip Editor into the white square of the fill tool fills the area with that chip.

Once the room is created, save it from the File menu, place it in your project folder, and load it via script.

Character Editor

The Character Editor creates characters (players, enemies, shopkeepers, etc.).



In "Unit Name", specify a unique name for the character.
Duplicate character names cannot be used.

In "Spawn Rate", higher values increase the likelihood of appearance.

For "Type", you can select types added via the "Define Character Types" button.
This type is also used for special effects on weapons and armor.
Other settings serve as the character's parameters.

The Special Abilities tab allows you to specify special abilities for the character.
Multiple special abilities can be assigned; however, due to the vast number of combinations, comprehensive testing has not been completed, so please report any bugs.

In Special Abilities, you can specify "Duration (Turns)", but if this value is not specified, the special ability will not trigger properly (more accurately, it triggers but recovers instantly).

Once the character is created, save it from the File menu, place the generated file in your project folder, and load it via script.

Similarly, open the Type window displayed via the "Character Type" button and save it.
As character types will be saved, place this file in your project folder as well.
Character types are automatically loaded when characters are loaded.

Item Editor

The Item Editor creates items.



"Type" is required to specify names for unidentified items.
You can add types using the "Type" button.

In "*.asd/*.asdx Label Name Executed When Item is Used", specify the animation label name to execute upon item usage.
This is the label name used to execute animations implemented in the character's *.asd/*.asdx.
Specifying [dir] in this value replaces it with the character's direction.
For example, specifying "*[dir]_eat" when the character is facing front will execute "*front_eat".



Special abilities include area attacks (all-target attacks), where you can specify an animation to play over damaged enemies.
If you create and assign an explosion animation, for example, the specified animation will play over the enemies taking damage.
It executes the animation specified in "*.asd/*.asdx Label Name Executed for Area Attack".

Additionally, when items are sorted, they are sorted according to their order in the left pane.
You can adjust the order using the "Å™" or "Å´" buttons.

As with the Character Editor, a "Duration (Turns)" can also be specified for item effects.
If this value is not specified, the item effect will not trigger properly (more accurately, it triggers but recovers instantly).



You can specify unidentified names for items.
These can be set for each "Type".
Please add more unidentified names than the number of items for each specified type.
If there are insufficient unidentified names, duplicate names will occur.

Once items are created, save from the File menu, place the generated files in your project folder, and load them via script.
Similarly, save "Type" and "Unidentified Names" from the menu, place them in your project folder, and load them via script.

Trap Editor

The Trap Editor creates traps.


Two icons can be specified: "Icon 1" sets the appearance of the trap in an un-triggered state.
"Icon 2" specifies the appearance after the trap has been triggered.
This setting is used, for example, to switch to an opened hole icon when a pitfall trap is triggered.

In "Animation Image Filename Executed Upon Trap Activation", you can specify the trap's animation image.
In "*.asd/*.asdx Label Name Executed Upon Trap Activation", you can specify the animation label name.
The *.asd/*.asdx file loaded will share the same filename as the image file.
For example, if loading "explosion_anim.png", it loads "explosion_anim.asdx".

Status effects caused by traps last for the number of turns specified in "Duration (Turns)".
If not specified, the effect will not trigger properly (more accurately, it triggers but recovers instantly).

Once traps are created, save from the File menu, place the generated file in your project folder, and load it via script.
